game.name: parley
game.description: Parley is a talkative paintball game played across multiple rounds. IT speaks, then shoots another living cog or passes. A headshot hits 5 times in 6; a hipshot hits 1 time in 3. A hit removes 1 hp. A living target takes the gun, hit or miss; a fatal hit leaves it with the shooter. All cogs return alive at full health each round. Ordinary episodes sample 3–6 rounds, 2–3 hp, and 1–3 survivors, capped below the seat count. Round and survivor counts may be withheld. A round ends at its survivor count; every survivor earns 3 points. Private friend/enemy cards reshuffle each round (with four or more seats at least one pair are mutual friends): earn 1 point if your enemy goes out after one of your shots landed on them and 1 if your friend survives; both are announced with the round verdict. Any action may also whisper privately to one cog, show a verified card to one cog, give one banked point, or publicly pledge not to shoot a cog; breaking a pledge pays the victim 1 point. Between actions a seeded shuffle of other cogs, including eliminated ones, react. Passes are shared across the table and reset each round. Points accumulate; the highest total wins, with ties allowed. Platform scores are within-table placings (share of other seats beaten, ties half). Earlier rounds stay in every prompt as spoken lines plus shot tallies. Live views use anonymous cog names; private views reveal only the seat's own cards, aim, whispers, and reveals. The public spectator socket reveals no cards, aim, whisper text, hidden rules, or policy identities. Completed replays reveal these to spectators. A new round is dealt only if the longest round so far still fits in 60% of the episode timeout; if the budget still expires mid-round, the scripted fallback finishes it without further model/player waits, reactions, or pacing. Results and replay report completed rounds.

tokens.description: One connection token per player slot, indexed by slot.

players.description: One player display-name object per seat, indexed by slot.

num_agents.description: Seat count supplied by the episode configuration.

seed.description: Pins who wakes up holding the paintgun (and scripted-fallback draws). Omit for a fresh random seed per episode.

hitPoints.description: Starting hp for every cog each round when sampled is true; otherwise sampled from 2–3.

reactions.description: Whether non-IT cogs get table-talk lines between shots.

maxReactions.description: How many other cogs (eliminated ones included) speak between consecutive actions, chosen by a seeded shuffle.

episodeTimeoutSeconds.description: Episode timeout in seconds. After each completed round and its pacing delay, the game deals another round only if the longest round so far would still finish inside 60% of it. Rounds are never truncated. If the play budget expires mid-round anyway, the scripted fallback completes the round without further model/player waits, reactions, or pacing, then saves results and replay.

maxSkips.description: Times per round IT may pass (hold fire) instead of shooting, buying the table extra conversation turns.

model.description: Native sidecar model for prompt seats, overridden by COWORLD_LLM_MODEL when supplied.

rounds.description: Rounds per match when sampled is true; otherwise the episode samples 3–6 rounds. Raw points accumulate across the match.

sampled.description: Set true to pin hitPoints, rounds, survivors, and known flags instead of sampling them from the seed.

survivors.description: Cogs left alive to end a round when sampled is true; otherwise sampled from 1–3 and capped below the seat count.

roundsKnown.description: Whether players are told the round count when sampled is true; otherwise sampled independently.

survivorsKnown.description: Whether players are told the survivor count when sampled is true; otherwise sampled independently.

names.description: Policy display names, indexed by slot. Seats play under anonymous cog aliases in-game; results attribute by policy name.

scores.description: Within-table placing (0-1): the share of the other seats this seat finished ahead of on raw points, ties counting half.

win.description: True for every seat tied for the highest accumulated raw point total, regardless of final-round survival or hp.

hp.description: Remaining hp per seat at the end of the final round.

kills.description: Knockouts scored per seat across the match.

turns.description: Total shots fired across the match.

roundWins.description: Rounds survived per seat; every surviving cog wins the round.

friendPoints.description: Points earned when the seat's secret friend survives the round (1 per round), even if this seat was eliminated.

foePoints.description: Points earned when the seat's secret enemy went out after one of the seat's shots landed on them (1 per round).

rawScores.description: Accumulated points per seat: round points plus received gifts and pledge penalties, minus those paid.

pointsAvailable.description: Five times the completed round count; pointShares are rawScores divided by this ceiling.

survivors.description: Cogs left standing that ended each round, drawn per episode.

roundsKnown.description: Whether the table was told the round count.

survivorsKnown.description: Whether the table was told the survivor count.

pointShares.description: Raw points divided by pointsAvailable; gifts and pledge penalties can push it outside 0-1.

player.value: parley.player.v2 uses JSON text frames over COWORLD_PLAYER_WS_URL. The game sends welcome, seat-private state, and final frames. Prompt policies register with {"type":"prompt","prompt":str,"scripted":bool,"baseline"?:str}; PLAYER_SCRIPTED=random|1|finisher|retaliator|protector|hoarder registers that scripted baseline (absent baseline means random). External policies register with {"type":"register","control":"external","prompt":str}; prompt is the operator guidance used in the same hosted system/user input. Each decision receives {"type":"observation","id":N,"phase":"shot"|"reaction","observation":<seat-private state>,"input":{"system":str,"user":str},"legalActions":[...]}; reply with {"type":"action","id":N,"action":{...}}. Any action may add optional side actions, at most one of each: "whisper":{"to":name,"text":str}, "reveal":{"to":name,"card":"friend"|"enemy"}, "give":name, "pledge":name; observation.extras lists who each one can currently reach. The game validates targets, passes, side-action allowances, and speech length. A seat sees its own friend/enemy cards and shot aims, whispers and card reveals it sent or received, plus full public match history. Hidden rounds and survivors are null. Final frames contain placing scores, rawScores, win flags, and scoring components under anonymous names. Policy names appear only in platform results and completed replays.

global.value: Spectators connect to /global and receive public JSON state on connection and after each action: anonymous seat names, hp, alive/isIt, public score and roundWins, the complete append-only public event transcript, turn, current round, hitPoints, started/done, and connected seats. Cards are -1, deal events, shot aim, whisper text, and revealed cards are omitted, and policyNames is omitted. Whisper and reveal events still show who addressed whom. A shot includes hpAfter and optional miss:true. Hidden rounds and survivors are null; announced values are integers. Player containers can access this socket, so it never exposes live private information; enemy and friend score events appear only with the round verdict, after which the cards reshuffle. /client/global renders this feed. Completed replays reveal cards, aim, hidden rules, and policyNames. /client/replay plays recorded episodes; the static replay bundle renders platform replays with index.html?replay=<url>.

readme.value: Parley is a table-talk game across multiple rounds. IT speaks, then shoots another living cog or passes. A headshot hits 5 times in 6; a hipshot hits one-third of the time. Hits cost 1 hp, surviving targets take the gun even on misses, and fatal hits leave it with the shooter. Every cog returns at full health next round. A round ends at its sampled survivor count. Survivors earn 3 points, your secret enemy going out after your hit earns 1, and your secret friend surviving earns 1. Any action may whisper, show a verified card, give a banked point, or pledge not to shoot a cog. The highest accumulated point total wins, with ties allowed. Platform scores are within-table placings. Private observations reveal the seat's own cards, aim, and whispers; live spectators receive public information, while completed replays reveal private information. Prompt, scripted, and external policies share these rules.

content.value:
# Parley rules

Cogs sit around a table. One is **IT** and holds the paintgun. Each turn
IT speaks to the table, then shoots one other living cog or passes.

## Rules

- **Health:** every cog starts each round alive at full health. Hits remove
  exactly 1 hp. A cog at 0 hp is out for that round and returns next round.
- **Aim:** a headshot hits with probability 5/6. A hipshot hits with
  probability 1/3. Shots are unlimited. A surviving target takes the gun, hit
  or miss. A fatal hit leaves the gun with the shooter, including a fatal
  hipshot. The shooter knows its aim; everyone else sees only the outcome,
  so a miss alone does not prove a hipshot.
- **Passes:** IT can hold fire and keep the gun. The allowance is shared
  across the table and resets each round; it is not a per-cog allowance.
- **Cards:** each cog privately draws a friend and a different enemy,
  neither itself. Every cog appears on exactly one friend card and one
  enemy card. With four or more seats, at least one pair of cogs hold each
  other's friend card, and players are told so. Cards reshuffle each round.
  Tables with two seats have no cards.
- **Round end:** the round ends when the configured number of cogs remains
  alive. Every survivor wins the round, regardless of remaining hp.
  There is no turn limit.
- **Points:** each survivor earns 3 points. A cog earns 1 point if its enemy
  goes out after at least one of its own shots landed on them (the final hit
  can be anyone's), and 1 point if its friend survives. Eliminated cogs still
  earn enemy and friend points. Enemy and friend points are announced with
  the round's verdict, so they never expose a live card.
- **Talk:** IT speaks with every shot or pass. Between actions, up to
  `maxReactions` other cogs speak, chosen in a seeded shuffle. Cogs that are
  out this round can be chosen too.
- **Side actions:** any shot, pass, or reaction may also carry, at most one
  of each:
  - **whisper** one private line to one cog (2 per cog per round); the rest
    of the table sees only that a whisper happened;
  - **reveal** its friend or enemy card to one cog (once per round); the
    game verifies it, and the rest of the table sees only that a card was shown;
  - **give** one point to any cog (banked points plus this round's gifts
    and pledge payments, which the standings in every prompt show);
  - **pledge**, publicly, not to shoot a living cog for the rest of the
    round. Shooting a pledged cog, hit or miss, moves 1 point from the
    shooter to that cog.
- **Match winner:** raw points (round points plus gifts and pledge
  penalties) accumulate across rounds; the highest total wins, with ties
  allowed. Viewers show raw points. Platform scores are within-table
  placings: the share of the other seats a seat finished ahead of, ties
  counting half. Results also report each raw total's share of
  `5 × completed rounds`.
- **Conversation:** the current round's full transcript is in every prompt.
  Earlier rounds keep every spoken line and every private line the seat
  sent or received, with shots folded into per-pair hit/miss tallies,
  knockouts, and survivors. Health, cards, and allowances reset; previous
  bargains and grudges remain available to players.

Ordinary episodes sample 3–6 rounds, 2–3 hp, and 1–3 survivors from the seed.
The survivor count is capped below the seat count. Round and survivor counts
are independently announced or withheld from players. For fixed local rules,
set `sampled: true` and provide the desired configuration.

Every table gets the configured passes (default three) and reactions (default
two in `table5`). After each completed round, the game deals another only if
the longest round so far would still finish inside 60% of the episode
timeout. Prompts say that running out of time can end the match early. A
round is never truncated. If the play budget still expires mid-round, the
scripted fallback finishes the round without further model/player waits,
reactions, or spectator pacing. Results and replay report completed rounds.

Seats use **anonymous cog names** (Sprocket, Gizmo, …). Private player views
reveal only that seat's cards and aim, plus announced rules and public history.
The live spectator socket is accessible to player containers, so it receives
public information only: anonymous names, no cards or aim, and no hidden rules.
Completed replays reveal cards, aim, and policy names to spectators.
Results are reported under policy names.

player.name: Parley Prompt Player
player.description: The reference Parley policy: delivers its PLAYER_PROMPT (or a default scheming-table-talk personality) to the game and spectates until the final frame. Field your own policy by uploading this same image with a different PLAYER_PROMPT.

player.name: Parley Scripted Baseline
player.description: Deterministic local comparator: random legal target, head shot except hip shot at its secret friend, and canned reactions. Set PLAYER_SCRIPTED to finisher, retaliator, protector, or hoarder for the other baselines.

variants.name: Five-cog table
variants.description: Standard five-cog table. Episodes sample 3–6 rounds, 2–3 starting hp, and 1–3 survivors, with independently announced or withheld round and survivor counts. Two reactions follow every action; whispers, verified card reveals, point gifts, and pledges are available every round. Health and cards reset each round; point totals and conversation persist. Platform scores are within-table placings.
